Beállítom Történetében először főtájépítészt keres a MÁV-csoport. A pozícióra olyan szakembert keresnek, aki stratégiai szemlélettel irányítja a vasúti zöldfelületek kezelését, összehangolja a vasútbiztonsági, ökológiai és környezetvédelmi szempontokat, és segít kialakítani egy korszerű, fenntartható zöldfelület-gazdálkodást – jelentette be Facebook-oldalán Vitézy Dávid közlekedési és beruházási miniszter. Vitézy azt írta, ideje újragondolni a vasút menti zöldterületek kezelését, és bár a vasútbiztonság nem lehet vita tárgya, meg kell vizsgálni, hogy a jelenlegi szabályok valóban minden esetben indokoltak-e. A miniszter azt írta, a MÁV-csoport Magyarország egyik legnagyobb zöldfelület-vagyonát kezeli a vasúti pályák és állomások mentén. Ezek fenntartása egyszerre közlekedésbiztonsági, természetvédelmi, városképi és klímavédelmi feladat. A miniszter hangsúlyozta, „nem a vasútbiztonság rovására szeretnénk több zöldfelületet, hanem a 21. századi szakmai tudásra, a fák mai ökológiai értékére építve szeretnénk felülvizsgálni azokat a szabályokat, amelyek ma már indokolatlan fakivágásokhoz vezethetnek. Ehhez pedig kiváló és innovatív szemlélettel rendelkező szakemberekre van szükségünk.” Vitézy azután kérte meg a MÁV-ot, hogy vizsgálja felül a teljes zöldfelület-kezelési gyakorlatát, miután a héten nagy port kavart, hogy a vasúttársaság a hőségriadó alatt vasúti töltésen lévő fákat vágott ki Zuglóban . A miniszter azonnal leállíttatta a munkát. A főtájépítészi pozícióra augusztus végéig lehet jelentkezni. https://nineoclock.ro/romanian-navy-day-.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount BUCHAREST — The Nine O’Clock editorial office received information from Romania’s Ministry of National Defence (MoND) regarding the events organised on Saturday, August 15, to mark Romanian Navy Day in Constanta and other cities across the country. The Romanian Naval Forces celebrated Romanian Navy Day on Saturday in Constanta, Mangalia, Braila, Tulcea, Galati and Bucharest. The main events took place in Constanta, along the seafront and in the maritime area in front of the Fleet Command headquarters. Starting at 10:00 a.m., more than 3,500 Romanian and foreign military personnel participated in the military ceremony and the joint and inter-institutional naval exercise FNR 26.10. More than 50 ships and boats and 15 military and civilian aircraft took part in the exercise, alongside land-based assets belonging to structures within Romania’s national defence, public order and national security system. This year’s edition marked the first participation of the “Contraamiral August Roman” corvette (261) and the M 271 “Capitan Constantin Dumitrescu” minehunter, which recently entered service with the Romanian Naval Forces. Military ships and aircraft from Turkey, Bulgaria, Spain and France also participated in the activities. FNR 26.10 included mine-countermeasure and anti-submarine warfare sequences, air defence operations, the repelling of a maritime landing, measures to combat illegal migration, as well as search-and-rescue missions at sea. The programme began with the traditional arrival of Neptune, the God of the Sea, followed by sailors’ games on the seafront and the opening salute performed by the Contraamiral August Roman corvette. The Romanian Navy Day celebrations are scheduled to conclude at 8:00 p.m. with a concert performed by the Romanian Naval Forces Military Band, followed by a torchlight procession by military sailors along the route Casino – Ovidiu Square – the seafront in front of the Fleet Command building. Between 9:30 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., Constanta City Hall will organise a laser and light show in the northern area of the Tomis breakwater. https://www.dw.com/en/integration-of-imm.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PLgX Prefer DW on Google Nurses Lais Oliveira from Brazil and Thi Theu Nguyen from Vietnam are examples of successful immigration Image: Markus Scholz/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate new arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems? Every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter. Since last year, that role has been held by Natalie Pawlik, a parliamentary representative from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD). Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed. They rightly expect that people who live in Germany permanently will learn our language and abide by our laws." The Commissioner for Integration is part of the Federal Ministry of Labor because ensuring that newcomers find work quickly is especially important. Employment rate of immigrants in Germany higher than in most EU countries The integration report was created by a team led by Frank Kalter, director of the German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM) , drawing on official government statistics, surveys and independent studies. They found that when all immigrant groups are counted, about 30% of the population today has some sort of migration background — even if that comes down to only one parent. Pawlik commented: "This is an important message at a time when the discussion often focuses primarily on problems related to supposedly failed integration." Kalter also pointed out that the employment rate among immigrants in Germany is higher than in most other EU countries — nearly 70%. And they work primarily in one sector: "In recent years, the biggest increase of workers without German citizenship has been in the health and social services sector." According to the data, there were about 1.8 million people without a German passport working in Germany in 2009. By 2025, this number had more than tripled to 5.8 million. Berlin initiative helps immigrant moms find their feet To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Concerns about unemployed mothers and violent youth However, there are still plenty of problems. In nearly all immigrant groups, women have difficulty finding employment, especially if they have children and their husbands are employed. Only about 60% of women in such families are employed, whereas nearly 88% of women in families with German passports are employed. There are also immigrant groups that face barriers to accessing educational opportunities and the job market. These are mostly young men who came to Germany as refugees. And if one considers citizenship as a distinguishing factor, the percentage of convicted criminals who are not German citizens is far higher — around 40% — than their share of the population. And they are also reported to the police far more frequently. At the same time, individuals without a German passport are also more likely to become victims of crimes. Germany relies on Syrian workers amid return debates To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Government cuts funding for integration courses Pawlik emphasizes that language acquisition is the foundation and starting point of any successful integration. But this is precisely where the government tightened its purse strings earlier this year in an effort to save money. Many integration courses are now no longer offered at all or receive less government funding. Pawlik made it clear that she is strongly critical of these cuts, even though she herself is part of the federal government. Most recently, Pawlik and her fellow Social Democrats have been advocating for people who have been working in Germany for some time to receive more secure residency permits — especially those from Syria and Ukraine . On Tuesday, SPD lawmakers adopted a position paper on the matter. In the paper, they propose that existing legal rights that allow workers to remain in the country should also apply to refugees. In other words, it would give working refugees a more secure status. But will the conservatives from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) — who lead the coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) — support this? "You'll have to ask the interior minister," Pawlik replied when asked by DW. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is known for being a hardliner on immigration policy.
